blocking.section: Decision outcome (ACK/NACK row, Reconnect row, Figure 2)
blocking.issue: An ACK can be lost, and the ADR has no way to recover it. The rules tie an ACK to one per-stream nonce. The stream can break after the Node activates but before its Ack reaches the Raft ACK bitmap: a replica crashes holding forwarded Acks, a leader fails over inside the 250 ms bitmap commit window, or the follower queue drops entries. When the Node reconnects, its Hello shows active digest equal to the assigned digest, so Figure 2 sends nothing and no Ack is ever produced. The Rollout engine then waits out the ACK timeout and retries, and the Node is quarantined as lagging even though it runs the right Revision. A replica or leader failure during a batch can therefore push the lagging count past max(1, 5% of the batch) and roll back or pause a healthy Rollout. That undercuts the Decision drivers' claim that stale replies are recognizable and the chaos claim that reconnecting Nodes get only their planned Revision without false failures.
blocking.evidence: ACK/NACK row: "Every configuration message carries a `nonce`; `Ack` means active, not durable; `Nack` keeps the active Revision and carries `code` and `class`; stale nonces are ignored". Figure 2: `same{"Active digest equals the assigned digest?"}` -> `none["Send nothing, HeartbeatReply carries the promotion"]`. Owning document, Replica roles: "Followers forward `Ack` and `Nack` at once and heartbeat aggregates every 5 s (target) through a bounded queue that drops the oldest"; Rollout plan: "ACKs commit as bitmaps every 250 ms (target)".
blocking.fix: Make the ACK record level-triggered, the same way Last-Known-Good promotion already is. Add to the ACK/NACK row: "Ruralz Control records an ACK per (`node.id`, `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`), not per stream. A `Hello` or `Heartbeat` whose active digest, `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq` match the Node's pending assignment counts as its `Ack`, so a lost `Ack` never makes a Node lag." Label Figure 2's 'Send nothing' branch as recording the implicit ACK. Add a container-free test to Confirmation: kill the replica holding a forwarded Ack before the bitmap commit, and the Node is still counted ACKed after it reconnects.

blocking.issue: The rationale depends on a milestone order that is wrong. The Control Stream is Planned (M2). gRPC ingress through connect is Planned (M3), so `ruralzd` does not 'already' link connect when the Control Stream ships: the Control Stream is what brings connect into both binaries. grpc-go is also linked into `ruralzd` for upstream clients from M3, so by M3 `ruralzd` carries both libraries under either option. The difference that actually decides the choice is on `ruralz-control`: one `net/http` HTTP/2 server with connect, against grpc-go's native server or its limited `ServeHTTP`. 'It adds no RPC library' holds only for the catalog, not for either binary.
blocking.evidence: Decision outcome: "and it adds no RPC library." Consequences: "Good, because `ruralzd` already links connect for gRPC ingress and `ruralz-control` serves it on `net/http`, so no second RPC library or HTTP/2 server appears." Tech stack library catalog: gRPC ingress `connectrpc.com/connect` ... "Planned (M3)"; gRPC upstream client grpc-go ... "Planned (M3)". System overview: "gRPC via `connectrpc.com/connect`, WebSocket, SSE Planned (M3)".
blocking.fix: In the Decision outcome, replace "it adds no RPC library" with "it uses the catalog's connect for every Ruralz-authored RPC and needs no second HTTP/2 server in `ruralz-control`". Rewrite the Consequences bullet as: "Good, because connect, the catalog's gRPC ingress library (Planned (M3)), enters both binaries with the Control Stream at Planned (M2) and gRPC ingress reuses it later; `ruralz-control` serves 8091 on `net/http`, so it runs no second HTTP/2 server."

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Delivery row, ACK/NACK row, Figure 2)
blocking.issue: A Node whose base content is corrupted can never recover. Ruralz Control cannot reproduce a Delta digest mismatch from the Revision, so under the ADR's own rule it counts as transient and is retried. The Figure 2 tree picks the transport only from the size of the change from the active digest. The retry is therefore the same Delta, which fails the same way until the Node is quarantined. The owning document reconciles RZ-CFG-027 with a Snapshot, and the ADR contradicts it by leaving that fallback out.
blocking.evidence: Delivery row: "`Delta` (`baseDigest`, `ops`) is used when the change encodes within 1 MiB (target), and a result that mismatches the digest is `Nack` RZ-CFG-027". ACK/NACK row: "a deterministic `Nack` fails the gate once Ruralz Control reproduces it, else it counts as transient". Figure 2: `small{"Change encodes within 1 MiB (target)?"}` -- yes --> `delta`. Owning document, Drift detection: "Local tampering | ... | `Nack` RZ-CFG-027, audit event | `Snapshot`; repeats quarantine".
blocking.fix: Append to the Delivery row: "after a `Nack` RZ-CFG-027 for a `Delta`, or a `Hello` whose Last-Known-Good or active content fails re-hash, the next delivery to that Node is a full `Snapshot`". In Figure 2, add a decision before 'small' ("Last Delta to this Node NACKed RZ-CFG-027?" yes -> snap). Extend the Confirmation integration test from "a mismatching `Delta` NACKed with RZ-CFG-027" to "... and followed by a `Snapshot` that the Node ACKs".

non_blocking.suggestion: Define 'configuration message' for a chunked Snapshot: all chunks of one nonce count as one message. Say what happens when a newer assignment arrives mid-Snapshot: the replica finishes it and supersedes it, or aborts it with a reset nonce. 'A newer assignment replaces an unsent one' does not cover a Snapshot that is partly sent.

Specify nonce uniqueness across replicas and reconnects (for example, 128-bit random, or derived from `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq` and a stream ID). Otherwise a new replica can reuse a value that `lastNonce` in `Hello` treats as already seen.

State what happens to duplicate streams for one `node.id`: during an ADR-0015 handover, or while a half-open stream on another replica has not yet been caught by HTTP/2 pings. A newer authenticated stream should supersede older ones, and ACK state should be keyed by `node.id` and sequence, not by stream (see L1-1).

`ReadTimeout` and `WriteTimeout` are server-wide on `http.Server`, so disabling them on 8091 also removes them from the unauthenticated unary `Enroll`. Keep `ReadHeaderTimeout` and `IdleTimeout`, and set per-request deadlines for `Enroll` with `http.ResponseController`, alongside `WithRequestGate` and the 16 KiB cap.

The 5-minute (target) largest-batch figure silently assumes a Snapshot size and a number of stream-serving replicas. Cite the owning document's 20 Snapshots/s per replica (hypothesis) and a typical Snapshot size, or state that most deliveries are Deltas. Also note that 10,000 Nodes at about 5,000 streams per replica (hypothesis) leaves no headroom when one of two serving replicas is down, so N+1 sizing applies.

Pack 8.2 says every snapshot and delta carries the promoted digest, and the owning document's `Snapshot` and `Delta` rows include `promotion`. Figure 1's Snapshot and Delta labels and the Delivery row mention only the HeartbeatReply; add `promotion` to them.

Say that a Node checks `totalBytes` against its derived Snapshot limit before buffering any chunk (OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-25). This bounds Node memory for chunked Snapshots and does not depend only on the 2 MiB per-message cap.

grpc-go is a catalog module (upstream client), so dependency admission does not stop `grpc.NewServer` in `ruralz-control`. Add a depguard or forbidigo rule that bans grpc-go server APIs under `cmd/ruralz-control` and the control packages, alongside the review checklist item.

non_blocking.section: Pros and cons of the options (Node polling)
non_blocking.suggestion: "no nonce ties an ACK to one delivery" is a weak con, because a poll response could carry `assignmentSeq` just as the stream does. Lead instead with the real costs: delivery latency tied to the poll window, no server-side pacing or `Reconnect`, and one extra fetch per delivery.
